title: Should you sell options right now? Read the IV vs RV chart
summary: Option sellers focus on strike, delta and expiration, but forget the first question: should I sell options at all right now? Plot implied volatility against realized volatility. When IV is well above RV, it is a good time to sell. When IV is low or even below RV, as in a trough, it is a bad time to sell and a better time to buy options.

steps.caption: The stock path over about two years.
The solid line: implied volatility, what you are paid.
Realized volatility: the risk you actually take.
Where IV is well above RV, it is a good time to be an option seller.
In the troughs IV is low or below RV. Then it is a bad time to sell; you would rather buy options.

takeaways: Ask whether to sell options at all before choosing strike or delta.
Sell when IV is well above realized volatility.
When IV is at or below RV, consider buying options instead.
caveats: The speaker's chart and metric behind the bio link are promotional and not verified here.
